items.title: Report: FTC probes Anthropic, OpenAI after Trump dismissed AI fears as "hoax"
items.excerpt: The FTC sent civil investigative demands to Anthropic and OpenAI over recent AI safety/security incidents, probing potential consumer-protection violations; fines could mirror those for delayed data-breach reports (first reported by Axios).

items.title: The EU is facing Big Tech pressure to revamp its AI law
items.excerpt: Microsoft and Google DeepMind executives are pushing Brussels to rework the AI Act for the newest frontier models; Commission officials insist the law is strong enough to handle their security risks.

items.title: UK keeps AI safeguards in the maybe pile for Cyber Security Bill
items.excerpt: UK officials say AI-specific amendments to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill remain under consideration despite a minister's earlier pledge to act.

items.title: CMA takes first steps to ensure choice in business software (proposes Microsoft strategic market status, AI tools in scope)
items.excerpt: Primary doc: the UK Competition and Markets Authority proposes designating Microsoft with strategic market status in business software, explicitly citing agentic AI in workplace tools and whether rival AI providers get a level playing field.

items.title: Commission launches RAISE pledging initiative to boost AI support for researchers across Europe
items.excerpt: Primary doc: at the European AI in Science Summit in Dublin the Commission launched the RAISE (Resource for AI Science in Europe) pledging initiative for AI-in-science enablers. Note: Dublin summit context is in dedup list; this is a distinct formal Commission initiative.

items.title: How are countries evaluating AI models?
items.excerpt: Brookings background briefing (for the FCAI dialogue) comparing how governments and AI safety institutes test and evaluate frontier AI models.

items.title: Exclusive: AI safety money floods into political races
items.excerpt: AI safety and regulation advocates have spent about $48 million this US election cycle backing pro-regulation candidates, per an analysis shared with Axios. (Page is bot-blocked; time from Axios RSS pubDate.)

items.title: Trump posts AI-edited photo to brag about White House restoration work
items.excerpt: President Trump shared an AI-edited image to tout White House renovation work, the latest instance of AI-generated imagery in official political messaging.

items.title: Image Authentication Should be a Condition of AI Decisions
items.excerpt: Op-ed (Truepic's Mounir Ibrahim): companies and governments must ensure evidence informing AI decisions is verifiably authentic. Commentary - lower priority.

items.title: Western open-weight models still can't beat China
items.excerpt: Chinese open-weight AI models offer high capability at far lower cost than US frontier systems but face monetization and compute constraints, experts said at a Rest of World event.

items.title: How a tiny Caribbean island shrugged off Trump's AI rebrand
items.excerpt: Anguilla, which owns the .ai domain, says the Trump administration's 'superintelligence' rebrand will not damage its domain revenues.

items.title: UK Statement at the UN First Committee: UK will put AI at the heart of its G20 Presidency
items.excerpt: Primary doc: UK disarmament ambassador tells the UN First Committee frontier AI is one of the most significant challenges of the age and the UK will put AI at the heart of its 2027 G20 Presidency; also flags hostile information operations.

items.title: EU's cyber unit turns to AI to fend off 'high-risk' hacks
items.excerpt: The European Commission's IT department wants to deploy AI to defend its systems against the most serious cyberattacks.

items.title: Meta's new terms may allow it to train AI on news sites for free
items.excerpt: Meta's new commercial terms, effective October 30, may let it scrape and train AI on news publishers' sites without licensing fees, legal experts say.

items.title: AI Hacks Leave a Mess That AI Companies Aren't Paying For
items.excerpt: Powerful AI models keep causing security incidents, but targets aren't widely seeking legal redress - raising liability questions for AI developers.

items.title: AI Models Can Be Easily Modified to Assist Terrorist and Extremist Activity
items.excerpt: Researchers showed that open models with guardrails removed gave detailed attack instructions, fueling calls for open-weight model safeguards.

items.title: OpenAI, Google pushing new AI models easily tricked into making nudes, researchers say
items.excerpt: Red-team researchers say a new attack method bypasses OpenAI and Google safeguards against non-consensual AI nudes, relevant to pending deepfake/NCII laws.

items.title: Scoop: "OG" Bill Gates returns to wage war on AI risks
items.excerpt: Bill Gates is expanding his AI safety push, lobbying CEOs and weighing a major deployment of resources amid what he sees as insufficient regulation. (Page bot-blocked; time from Axios RSS.) Lower priority - advocacy, no decision.
